title: Women's rights and suffrage
summary: In 1848 a convention at Seneca Falls, New York, resolved that women should secure the elective franchise. Sweden gave some women local votes in 1862, and New Zealand's Electoral Act of 1893 made it the first self-governing nation to give women the national vote. American women won it in 1920, after decades of struggle, and women in France and Italy at the end of World War II. Switzerland followed in 1971 and Liechtenstein in 1984. Saudi Arabia was the last, in December 2015.

as_recorded.value: The last country to extend voting rights to women was Saudi Arabia, in December of 2015
